citations.narrative:
A non-human primate suffered a fatal injury while being handled for a medical procedure. On 4/16/25 a female
cynomolgus macaque (DB849) evaded 2 animal care technicians and escaped her enclosure. She ran down the central
aisle toward an exhaust fan, where she tried to crawl through the open slates and sustained a severe head injury from the
moving fan blades. Due to the severe head trauma, the animal was euthanized. Animals that are not handled carefully
can become distressed and injured, including death. Handling of all animals shall be done as expeditiously and carefully
as possible in a manner that does not cause trauma, overheating, excessive cooling, behavioral stress, physical harm, or
unnecessary discomfort. Correct from 4/16/26 forward.

A primary enclosure in the facility did not protect a non-human primate from injury. On 7/10/25, a 16-year-old female
Rhesus Macaque (09D128) suffered from a transverse fracture of the tibia and fibula of the right leg and was eventually
euthanized on 8/1/25 after it was determined that the fracture was not healing and she would not do well with an
amputation. The fracture occurred when she wedged her right leg between the two round bars that make up a perch in
the enclosure. The two bars have clamps at regular intervals between the perch mounts to keep the bars aligned across
the length of the perch. It was determined that the clamps on the perch were of an older style that created a smaller gap
at the clamp point, creating a catch point where the limb became entrapped. All clamps of this style were removed from
each enclosure following this incident. Animals who are injured or entangled by their primary enclosure may experience
pain, injury, stress, and even death. Correct by ensuring that enclosures protect nonhuman primates from injury.
Corrected prior to date of inspection on 4/15/26
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
Additional Inspectors:
Lindsay Livingston, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
